speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are experiencing agitation, yellowing of your skin and eyes, and abnormal lab results; to determine the cause, have you recently consumed any large amounts of shellfish or raw oysters?

speaker: Patient
text: 20-year-old male. The patient was previously healthy and has been brought to the emergency department due to agitation over the past 24 hours. Family members have noticed a yellowish coloring of his skin and eyes over the past week. The patient has a history of occasional cocaine and ecstasy use, and drinks alcohol socially on weekends. The patient also admits to high-risk sexual behaviors without using appropriate protection.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Hepatitis C infection (acute/subacute) leading to acute liver failure.

Given your history of high-risk sexual behavior and the rapid onset of jaundice and agitation, it is highly likely you have contracted Hepatitis C. Cocaine use can also cause liver damage or mimic these symptoms, but the timeline and risk factors point strongly toward a viral etiology. Do you have any other symptoms like nausea, vomiting, or severe abdominal pain?
